speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. These symptoms are concerning for a significant underlying condition; have you noticed if the lymph nodes are hard, fixed to surrounding tissue, or painful to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those "drenching" night sweats combined with 12 pounds of weight loss and four weeks of worsening abdominal pain are alarming "B symptoms." Have you noticed any change in your bowel habits or stool color recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of fixed, non-tender, enlarging supraclavicular lymph nodes alongside constitutional symptoms like night sweats and significant weight loss is highly concerning for malignancy. Given the abdominal pain, have you noticed any jaundice, dark urine, or pale stools? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, LDH, and ESR.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma.

The clinical picture of B-symptoms, fixed supraclavicular nodes, splenomegaly, and a biopsy showing CD20-positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index is diagnostic for a B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, likely Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma.
